key: Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much.
s: As the clans lay siege and waverers seek leave, the besieged are pointed to the messenger; al-Tabari, on 33:21 to 33:22, reads it as reproaching believers who hung back: one hoping for God’s reward does not spare himself, but stays with him wherever he is.

evidence.words: وهذا عتاب من الله للمتخلفين عن رسول الله ﷺ وعسكره بالمدينة، من المؤمنين به، يقول لهم جلّ ثناؤه: ﴿لقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة﴾ : أن تتأسوا به وتكونوا معه حيث كان، ولا تتخلَّفوا عنه ﴿لِمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُو اللَّهَ﴾ يقول: فإن من يرجو ثواب الله ورحمته في الآخرة لا يرغب بنفسه، ولكنه تكون له به أُسوة في أن يكون معه حيث يكون هو.
evidence.gloss: This is a reproach from God to those believers who stayed behind from the Messenger of God and his camp at Medina. He says to them: in the Messenger of God you had a good example, that you model yourselves on him and be with him wherever he was and not stay behind; for whoever hopes for God’s reward and mercy in the hereafter does not hold his own life dearer, but takes him as an example in being with him wherever he is.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Ahzab 33:21, at 3553). al-Tabari comments on 33:21 to 33:22 as one segment; after the variant readings of uswa he says in his own voice that the ayah is a reproach to the believers who stayed behind from the Prophet and his camp, and that one hoping for God’s reward does not hold himself back but is with him wherever he is, then cites Ibn Ishaq to the same effect. The sentence paraphrases exactly that. Plain sense (the clans’ siege, 33:20 and 33:22; waverers seeking leave, 33:13) is faithful to day.js. Ibn Kathir and al-Qurtubi also read the example in the siege setting; al-Tabari as default is right. Entry-check ok, no changes.
